### What does this PR do?

Fixes the Triton fused linear cross-entropy (`verl/utils/kernel/kernels.py`, used with `use_fused_kernels=True`) so a confident label keeps its logprob and gradient. Before this change the forward formed `z_t - (max + log(accu))`, where `accu` sums `exp(z - max)` over every logit, including the label's own 1.0. Once the label's margin over the other logits passed ~16.6 in fp32, `accu` rounded to 1. The logprob and the label's gradient entry `exp_logits * accu_rcp - 1` both became exactly 0, while the other entries stayed nonzero. Part of #8376, which has a repro; the torch log-prob half is #8377.

Following Barron et al., "A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy" (arXiv:2610.31642), the logprob is now `-softplus((max - z_t) + log(accu_other))`. `accu_other` is accumulated with the label's term left out, rather than subtracted from `accu` afterwards.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Query links: [`linear_cross_entropy`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+linear_cross_entropy), [`entropy kernel`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+entropy+kernel), [`cross entropy precision`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+cross+entropy+precision)
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

**Why this does not duplicate an existing PR:** I searched open PRs and issues (the queries above, plus `softmax underflow`, `expm1`, `logprobs softplus`), and none changes how the kernel forms the label's logprob or gradient. Two open PRs touch the same files for other reasons, so whichever lands second will need a rebase:
- #7439 uses `-inf` as the max-reduction identity so all-negative logits stay shift invariant.
- #6110 adds per-sample temperature by pre-scaling the hidden states.

### Test

AI-assisted change, see the statement at the end. Run on an RTX 3090 with torch 2.9.1+cu128 and Triton 3.5.1:

```bash
pytest tests/utils/test_linear_cross_entropy.py -q
# 9 passed, 4 failed: the 4 _Total_Fuse_MN cases
# OutOfResources(131072, 101376, 'shared memory'), the same on main: the default MN backward tile needs more shared memory than a 3090 has
pytest tests/utils/test_linear_cross_entropy.py -q -p small_mn_tiles
# 13 passed
```

- **`small_mn_tiles`** is a local pytest plugin, not part of this PR. It restricts the `_Total_Fuse_MN` autotune configs to 64×64×32 tiles with 2 stages, so that backward fits on a 3090. A100/H100 runners shouldn't need it.
- **New tests** in `tests/utils/test_linear_cross_entropy.py` (run by `gpu_unit_tests.yml`), each parametrised over the three backward methods:
  - `test_lce_confident_labels[none|sum|mean]`: label margins of ~10–80 over V=20011 (not a multiple of any split size) against an fp64 reference, for logprobs and for the logit gradient, including the label entry. These fail on `main` and pass here.
  - `test_lce_matches_fp64_reference`: ordinary logits at T=1.5, where logprobs, entropy, and both gradients match fp64.
- **Issue repro** before and after (the gradient is bf16, hence 2.998e-09):
  ```
  main: logprob=-0.000e+00 label_grad=0.000e+00 other_grads_sum=-2.998e-09
  this: logprob=-2.994e-09 label_grad=2.998e-09 other_grads_sum=-2.998e-09
  ```
- **Large logit offsets:** with every logit offset by +700 (N=256, V=32000), the max logprob error vs fp64 is 1.3e-6, the same as at offset 0. Forming `max + log(accu_other)` before subtracting `z_t` gave 3.0e-5 there.
- **Bitwise comparison with `main`** at ordinary logits (N=1024, V=32003):
  - `maximum`, `accumulate`, and `entropy_b` are bitwise identical.
  - The non-TP entropy differs by 1 ulp (9.5e-7) on 25 of 1024 rows. The cause is codegen in the edited epilogue (FMA contraction), not a change to the formula; the max error vs fp64 is 1.248e-6 on both.
- **Tensor parallelism:** I couldn't run `test_special_linear_cross_entropy_tp.py`, which needs `WORLD_SIZE > 1`. With a 1-rank NCCL group passed as `dist_process_group`, the TP path's logprobs and `d_weight` are bitwise identical to the non-TP path and match fp64. Please run the 8-GPU TP test in CI.
- **Single token:** the non-TP epilogue on `main` fails to compile for `num_tokens == 1` (`num_tokens.to(tl.float32)` on a value Triton specialised to 1, see #8376). That line is gone here, and a single token now works.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes.

### API and Usage Example

No change to `linear_cross_entropy` or `LinearCrossEntropy`. The internal `kernels.efficient_entropy_forward` now returns one more tensor, `one_minus_p`, and `kernels.efficient_entropy_backward` takes it. `LinearCrossEntropy` is their only caller in the repo.

### Design & Code Changes

- **Forward mainloop:** also accumulates `accu_other`, the online sum of `exp(z - max)` with the label's term masked out before summing, stored per vocab split like `accu`.
- **Epilogues:** reduce `accu_other` across splits like `accu`. Under TP it rides in the existing all-reduce buffer for `accumulate` and `entropy_b` (now 3 × num_tokens), so there is no extra collective.
- **Host:** computes `logprob = -softplus((max - z_t) + log(accu_other))` and `1 - p_t = -expm1(logprob)` in torch, then applies the none/sum/mean reduction. Subtracting `z_t` from `max` first keeps the rounding at the scale of the margin rather than of the logits. The reduction moved out of the epilogue kernels, along with their `atomic_add` and the mainloop's scalar init store.
- **All five backward kernels:** take `1 - p_t` and use `-(1 - p_t)` for the label entry of `softmax - onehot`. The other entries and the entropy gradient are unchanged. The `d_hidden`/`d_weight`-only kernels are updated the same way but aren't launched by any current backward method, so no test covers them.
- **Entropy:** still uses the full `accu`.
- **TP label-logit buffer:** always zero-initialised now. It used to be `torch.empty` for `reduction="sum"/"mean"`, so non-owner ranks all-reduced uninitialised memory into the label logit.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting)
- [ ] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs). Not needed: no user-facing change beyond the numerics.
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. The exceptions are the two backward kernels no backward method launches, noted above.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` channel.

`760-760`: ** Trivial** · **Functional Correctness** · **Low value** **Subtract the label logit before adding `log(accumulate_other)`.** The expression evaluates as `(maximum + torch.log(accumulate_other)) - label_logits`. The first addition yields about the log-sum-exp of the non-label logits, which has the magnitude of those logits. Its rounding error is half an ulp at that magnitude: about 4e-6 for values in [64, 128) and about 3e-5 for values in [512, 1024). This error depends on the logit offset, and it enters `softplus` unchanged. When the label is the maximum, `maximum - label_logits` is exactly 0. When the two logits are within a factor of 2, Sterbenz's lemma makes their difference exact. Subtracting first removes the offset-dependent rounding at no extra cost. The remaining rounding occurs at the scale of the margin. The practical effect is small. It matters only for large logit offsets. At typical magnitudes, the existing rounding in `log(accumulate_other)` is comparable or larger. For confident labels, `one_minus_p = -expm1(token_logprobs)` changes very little, because its sensitivity to the log-probability is about `exp(token_logprobs)`.
